# The reference fixture project

BUILD_PLAN §3.7.5 (line 536) defines this directory: a **frozen, versioned,
~120-record synthetic Layer 0 archive, hand-built to exercise every edge**.
It is laid out exactly as `prismabib.capture.capture_search` writes a real
acquisition run (`src/prismabib/capture/writer.py`), so Stage 3's
`build_store(project, ...)` can consume it unmodified. It is what Stage 3's
golden test (`test_build_store__reference_fixture__table_checksums_match_golden`)
and every later stage's `e2e` test run against.

## The change rule (BUILD_PLAN §3.7.5, verbatim in substance)

**This fixture is frozen.** `raw/` is never hand-edited — it is only ever
produced by running `generate_reference_fixture.py`. Changing anything under
this directory (`project.toml`, `criteria.yaml`, or the generator, which
regenerates `raw/`) requires a pull request that:

1. **Explains why** the reference fixture needs to change — not just what
   changed. "Regenerated to add an edge case for risk N" is an explanation;
   "updated fixture" is not.
2. **Updates every affected golden snapshot in the same commit.** Stage 3's
   `test_build_store__reference_fixture__table_checksums_match_golden` and any
   `syrupy` snapshot that reads this fixture must be regenerated and reviewed
   alongside the fixture change — never in a follow-up PR, and never via
   `syrupy --snapshot-update` in CI (CI never runs that).

A PR that regenerates this fixture without explaining the diff is rejected,
exactly as BUILD_PLAN §3.7.5's final bullet says of golden snapshots
generally: this fixture *drives* those snapshots, so the same rule applies to
it one level up.

## Provenance and content policy

- **Shape matches reality.** Every field name, and every scalar-vs-list
  quirk, is checked directly against `tests/fixtures/cassettes/complete-page-0000.json`
  and `complete-page-0001.json` — the genuine, sanitised `view=COMPLETE`
  recordings that are this fixture's structural template. See
  `verify_reference_fixture.py`'s cassette-derivation check for the
  mechanical half of that claim (no title/DOI/ORCID/authid is shared), and
  the "Design notes" section below for the shape decisions themselves.
- **Content is synthetic.** No title, abstract, keyword, author name, ORCID,
  `authid`, `afid`, or DOI in `raw/` is copied from a cassette recording.
  Everything is generated by `generate_reference_fixture.py` from word banks
  and templates it owns.
- **Determinism.** `generate_reference_fixture.py` threads a single
  `random.Random(SEED)` through every generation step; `RUN_ID` and every
  timestamp/cursor token are hardcoded constants. Regenerating from a clean
  checkout reproduces `raw/` byte-for-byte — verified directly by
  `verify_reference_fixture.py`, and by running the generator twice and
  diffing (done as part of building this fixture; see the agent's
  verification transcript).

## Layout

```
tests/fixtures/projects/reference/
  project.toml                          # §3.1 shape; real [query] table
  criteria.yaml                         # §3.1 shape; version 1.0.0
  generate_reference_fixture.py         # the generator; commit alongside raw/
  verify_reference_fixture.py           # prints the evidence this README quotes
  raw/20260115T090000Z-fee5c0de/
    page-0000.jsonl                     # 25 entries
    page-0001.jsonl                     # 25 entries
    page-0002.jsonl                     # 25 entries
    page-0003.jsonl                     # 25 entries
    page-0004.jsonl                     # 20 entries (120 total)
    manifest.json                       # RunManifest, Stage 2 lines 787-800
  README.md                             # this file
```

Regenerate with:

```
uv run python tests/fixtures/projects/reference/generate_reference_fixture.py
uv run python tests/fixtures/projects/reference/verify_reference_fixture.py
```

## On `manifest.json`

- `total_results` is `120` — the record count in this fixture — and is the
  **only** source Stage 3 may read for the PRISMA "records identified"
  number (BUILD_PLAN line 807). A later test asserts nothing derives that
  count from a row count instead.
- `payload_sha256` is a real SHA-256 over the concatenation, in
  `payload_files` order, of the exact bytes of every `page-NNNN.jsonl` file
  — computed the same way `capture/writer.py`'s `_payload_sha256` computes
  it, so a Stage 3 provenance test can verify it rather than trust a
  placeholder. Recompute and compare with `verify_reference_fixture.py`.
- `manifest.json` itself is a real `prismabib.capture.manifest.RunManifest`,
  constructed and serialised by the generator via
  `RunManifest(...).model_dump_json(indent=2)` — the identical call
  `capture_search` itself makes — so its shape cannot drift from the frozen
  Stage 2 contract.
- `query` is produced by calling `prismabib.query.build_query_for_project`
  against this directory's own `project.toml`, so it is guaranteed to match
  what a real `capture_search()` run against this project would have sent,
  and it equals BUILD_PLAN §3.1's own worked example string.

## On `PayloadRef` / provenance

Each `page-NNNN.jsonl` file is written the same way
`capture/writer.py::_write_page` writes one: the **entire parsed page**
(the `search-results` envelope plus all of its `entry` records) is
serialised as a single compact JSON document and written as **one line**.
This means, for every record in this fixture, `PayloadRef.line` is always
`0` — there is only one line in the file it points to — and
`PayloadRef.resolve()` returns the whole page's raw JSON, not a
single-record slice. That still satisfies Stage 3's
`test_build_store__every_record__payload_ref_resolves` (BUILD_PLAN
S03-AC2): the resolved text is a valid JSON object, and the record itself is
locatable inside it by `dc:identifier`. The location table below therefore
gives both coordinates: the page file (`payload_file`, `payload_line` is
always `0`) **and** the record's position in that page's `entry` array,
which is what actually distinguishes it from its 24 (or 19, on the last
page) page-mates.

## The eight required edge cases

Locations below are exactly what `verify_reference_fixture.py` prints;
regenerate and re-run it before trusting a stale copy of this table.

| # | Edge case | `dc:identifier` | `payload_file` | entry index in page | Notes |
| - | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Record with no abstract | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000001` | `page-0000.jsonl` | 2 | `dc:description` key is entirely absent, matching real Scopus behaviour for the doc types that carry none (see `tests/fixtures/README.md`'s note on `complete-page-0000.json`'s 3 keyword/author-less entries). |
| 2 | Record with scalar `afid` | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000002` | `page-0000.jsonl` | 7 | Its affiliation object's `"afid"` is a bare string (`"60000009"`), not a list. Every other record in this fixture uses the list form (`["<id>"]`) instead, so this record is the one exercising `Affiliation._coerce_afid_scalar`'s pass-through (non-list) branch specifically — see "Design notes" below. |
| 3 | Non-English record | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000003` | `page-0001.jsonl` | 5 | `"language": "German"` (every other record: `"English"`); title and abstract are hand-authored German text, not templated, so it reads as genuinely non-English rather than English words shuffled. |
| 4 | Record with 40+ authors | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000004` | `page-0001.jsonl` | 15 | Exactly 45 authors; `author-count.$` is `"45"`. |
| 5 | Record with zero keywords | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000005` | `page-0002.jsonl` | 5 | `authkeywords` key is entirely absent (not an empty string), so a loader must not synthesise a phantom empty-string keyword. |
| 6 | Duplicate DOI, record A | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000006` | `page-0002.jsonl` | 10 | Shares `prism:doi = "10.1145/3609015.3609231"` with record B below. Different `record_id`s, different titles/authors — a same-source re-indexing, not a copy-paste. |
| 6 | Duplicate DOI, record B | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000007` | `page-0003.jsonl` | 15 | Same `prism:doi` as record A. Dedup must be *reported*, not silently applied, in a single-source project (BUILD_PLAN line 916). |
| 7 | 2026 partial-year record | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000008` | `page-0003.jsonl` | 20 | `prism:coverDate = "2026-01-05"`, i.e. within `project.toml`'s `retrieved_at = 2026-01-15T09:00:00Z` snapshot but before the year is complete — a subject for Stage 7's CAGR partial-year exclusion. |
| 8 | Unmapped country string | `SCOPUS_ID:900000000009` | `page-0004.jsonl` | 15 | `affiliation-country = "Korea"` — deliberately *not* one of the variants `prismabib.countries` recognises (it maps `"south korea"` and `"korea, republic of"`, but not bare `"korea"`), verified live against `normalise_country()` while building this fixture (see the agent's verification transcript). Exercises the warn-and-count-as-unknown path (BUILD_PLAN §5 risk 8). |

Every location above was produced by `verify_reference_fixture.py`
enumerating `raw/`'s actual pages, not hand-transcribed from the
generator's source — so if this table and the generator ever disagree, the
generator (and a re-run of the verify script) is the source of truth to
reconcile against.

## Design notes (for anyone extending or auditing this fixture)

- **Why 5 pages of 25/25/25/25/20.** `count=25` is the mandated COMPLETE-view
  page size (BUILD_PLAN line 765); 120 records is not a multiple of 25, so
  the last page is deliberately partial (20 entries) — the same shape a real
  `total_results = 120` run would produce, and a mild extra check that
  nothing in Stage 3 assumes every page is full.
- **`SCOPUS_ID` numbering is a deliberate, greppable convention, not
  arbitrary.** The 9 edge-case records live in the reserved
  `SCOPUS_ID:9000000000NN` block (`NN` = 01..09, in the table order above);
  every other record uses `SCOPUS_ID:2050470NNNNN`. Both blocks are disjoint
  from the real cassette recordings' IDs (which use a `105047NNNNNN` prefix),
  so there is no risk of an accidental collision reading as "derived from a
  real recording."
- **Scalar-vs-list `afid` distribution is inverted from the raw cassette on
  purpose.** In the two real COMPLETE-view cassette recordings, every
  affiliation-level `afid` observed is a bare scalar string (see
  `tests/fixtures/README.md`) — the list form is a documented Scopus quirk
  (`src/prismabib/models.py`'s `Affiliation._coerce_afid_scalar` docstring,
  `docs/architecture/data-model.md`'s "Affiliation afid scalar vs. list"
  section) that this particular recording session simply never triggered.
  To make sure both wire shapes are exercised by *this* fixture — and to
  make edge case #2 unambiguously locatable as "the one" — every record
  here except #2 uses the list form (`["<id>"]`) and only #2 uses the bare
  scalar. Functionally this is a no-op either way (both branches resolve to
  the same canonical id), but it means a loader that only ever sees the
  scalar branch (because it was only ever tested against the raw cassette)
  cannot silently pass this fixture too.
- **No `language` field appears in the real cassette recordings at all**
  (checked directly: zero of the 75 recorded entries across both
  COMPLETE-view cassette pages carry a `"language"` key). `Record.language`
  and `records.language` (Stage 3 schema) exist specifically so Stage 4's
  `engine.language_set()` has something to filter on, so this fixture adds a
  `"language"` field to every entry (`"English"` by default, `"German"` on
  edge case #3) as a forward-looking extension of the wire shape, not a
  cassette-observed field. If a later Stage 2 recording confirms Scopus's
  real key name/shape for this field differs, this fixture's `raw/` must be
  regenerated to match it — that is exactly the kind of change this file's
  "change rule" section above exists to gate.
- **Institutions, author names, titles, and keywords** are drawn from fixed
  word banks and name pools in `generate_reference_fixture.py`
  (`_INSTITUTIONS`, `_SURNAMES`, `_GIVEN_NAMES`, `_TITLE_WORDS`,
  `_KEYWORD_PHRASES`, etc.), combined via the seeded `random.Random`. None of
  these pools were copied from `tests/fixtures/cassettes/`.
- **Countries.** All institutions except edge case #8's resolve through
  `prismabib.countries.normalise_country` (checked directly against the real
  function while building this fixture), so the geography analysis has
  clean data to work with in the common case, with exactly one deliberate
  gap.

different from the block above, `raw/` has drifted from what this README
documents — regenerate it, re-run `verify_reference_fixture.py`, and update
this transcript (and the location table above it) in the same commit, per
the change rule at the top of this file.
